I'm an incoming sophomore at a top 5 public university in the US, and I had a few questions. I have shadowed orthopedic doctors several times and each time I have continually fallen in love with the work that they are doing. I am actively looking to study abroad, and I was wondering if studying abroad is an advisable option for a premed student. If I were to go abroad, I would probably do it in the fall of my junior year (2016), and while abroad I would definitely want to participate in volunteer work. Does anyone have any recommendations for an individual thinking about studying abroad, and would the timing of the study abroad impact an application to medical school? I am the first person in my family going through the pre-med process, and I am struggling to piece together my steps. Could anyone help me create a rough timeline of what the recommended steps are for applying to medical school (i.e. when one would study abroad-- if at all--, which year of college to plan on taking the mcat, when to take a gap year)

Thank you so much, any input would help me!

Man, that's a lot of questions. But you're the first in your family, as was I. So I have a soft spot.

Studying abroad is cool because it will give you something really interesting to talk about in your personal statement, your secondaries, and your interview. Go somewhere you love, and study things that interest you - you want your passion to show. The timing is fine.

You'll have to take the MCAT. It's a pain in the ass. Here's your study technique: do practice problems. All of them. Take all the tests. Take them twice. Take the MCAT the summer after your junior year.

Apply to med school at the end of your junior year. It's also a pain in the ass. Go see your premed advisor at your school about where you might apply. Caveat: premed advisors sometimes don't know what they're doing, especially if they actively discourage you. Sad, but true. If that's the case, be polite, but then go elsewhere for advice.

Where you apply is dependent largely on your MCAT, GPA, then also by your recommendations and personal background. You'll get secondaries because they want your money. If your scores are competitive, give them your money. There's a jillion places to find a "chance predictor." I'll post one here for sweet, sweet voats.

If all goes well, and you applied wisely, you'll get some interviews. Be yourself. Wear a suit. Cut your hair or something. You'll probably get some offers.

If you don't get some offers, now you have a Gap Year following your senior year. Do something interesting. It might be medical, it might not, but it should be interesting. And you should also do something medical. Volunteer with a hospice, maybe. Reapply the following year.

What you really need is a BOOK. Go on Amazon and buy Med School Confidential. Read it. Become wise.

Come back here with questions. Do not go to Student Doctor Network. If you go to Student Doctor Network, remember that everyone there lies. There's not that many people with 40 MCATs in the last five years.

You might go to some other website, too. /r/premed has a good FAQ in the sidebar. It just hasn't been stolen for /v/premed yet.

Good luck.

A good friend of mine was pre-med and is in medical school now and took a semester of their junion year off to study abroad. It's definitely doable!

Going during the Fall of Junior year is probably the best time in my opinion. The downsides are figuring out when to take the MCAT and getting all your class requirements.

As far as taking the MCAT goes, I'd assume you'd want to take it after going abroad. In that case I'd recommend aiming at the January or March dates, though January doesn't give much time to study post-abroad and March means you're taking it smack in the middle of a semester of classes.

Class requirements-wise, make sure you have all ayour major/premed stuff down and don't need that semester abroad at your home university to graduate on time.

Were you to take a gap year, it would be after graduating from your university. So four years of college, graduate, gap year doing something, and apply during that gap year.

If you do go abroad, I strongly recommend you try to find some cool medically-related experiences or opportunities while you're wherever you're going. They can look very unique which helps in the application process, and also provide a perspective that may be straight up impossible to get while back in the US, depending on where you're going.

I've got a Samsung Syncmaster 2232GW. I've had it for several years. Over the past couple months it's started having an issue where when I first turn it on for the day, it takes forever for the backlight to decide to stay on. It also started devloping an issue where even if the backlight had been staying on, it will go out if the image on the screen is supposed to be mostly dark. Turning it off and on repeatedly usually fixed it, but for a very short time. Eventually it got to the point where the backlight wouldn't come on at all.

After some searching I found that the most likely cause was a bad capacitor, so I opened it up and indeed, one capacitor on the power supply board was slightly bulged at the vent. I replaced the capacitor, put it all back together, and started it up again. The backlight was again working, but still exhibiting the issues of taking forever to stay on and of not staying on when the image is dark. I've taken it apart again since then but all the capacitors seem to be fine. I checked all the connections, all the solder joints, everything looks perfect.

Anyone have any other ideas? It seems to be getting worse and I have a feeling it's going to go out complete again soon, and I can't afford a new monitor.

<Also I don't know if or how it's related, but when the backlight went out a little bit earlier today and I turned it off and on, the monitor displayed bright white and light grey snow, like what you'd see when an old TV's cable is disconnected. I don't have a TV input on the monitor or on my PC, so I have no idea what that's about. It went away after another power cycle.>

It's just suddenly gotten a lot worse, even a small black window surrounded by a mostly white screen is doing it now.

Strange thing is if I change the input to analog where it has no input, which just shows a black screen with a tiny white and blue window, that displays fine.
Did you make sure to use the right type of capacitor, in the proper polarity?
